about.summary:
It all started in college. That’s where I wrote my first “Hello World” program in Java using Eclipse. It may seem like just another line of code, but I clearly remember the thrill of seeing a program I’d created actually work. That small moment sparked something that, over time, would become an important part of my professional life. As I progressed through my degree, I discovered another world that would change the way I understood development: databases.

I learned to use MySQL from the command line, writing SQL queries and understanding how data could be stored, related, and retrieved. Soon after, I discovered PHP, HTML, and CSS, and that’s when many pieces began to fall into place. For the first time, I could connect an application to a database and turn it into a dynamic system. User interfaces began to breathe life into what I was building, and I discovered something that remains important to me to this day: I still enjoy creating solutions that not only work but also provide a great user experience. That’s how web development began to become the path I wanted to continue exploring.

During my training, I also had the opportunity to experiment with different areas of software development. I learned how to use Android Studio and Ionic to develop native and hybrid mobile apps.

I also took my first steps with Python and data analysis using Pandas. At the time, it was mainly an introduction, but it ended up sparking a curiosity that has grown over the years. I’m currently delving deeper into Python and the development of solutions related to artificial intelligence, seeking to understand how these technologies can be used to solve real-world problems and optimize processes.

Another experience I remember particularly well was working with Arduino. Building small circuits on a breadboard, controlling LEDs, and seeing how the software could interact directly with the hardware was a completely different way of understanding programming. It allowed me to discover another facet of this profession and appreciate its versatility even more.

Finally, I took my first steps with Linux. Although I started out with simple tasks and basic commands, that experience allowed me to become familiar with an environment that would eventually become an essential tool in software development.

After completing my studies, I had the opportunity to begin my professional career in web development using WordPress. At first, I worked mainly with visual builders, but over time I moved on to customizing themes and plugins using code. I also participated in optimizing live websites, as well as in their ongoing maintenance and support.

This experience allowed me to work on projects for various clients and collaborate closely with senior developers, designers, and project managers. Beyond technical knowledge, it was an important phase for developing skills that I consider essential in any software project: communication, teamwork, the ability to analyze problems, and the responsibility to ensure that solutions continue to function properly once they go into production.

I have also had the opportunity to work both remotely and in person, adapting to different work dynamics and ways of collaborating. I continue to particularly enjoy web development and am open to participating in projects in this field. At the same time, I have begun to delve deeper into Python and artificial intelligence, particularly how these technologies can be used to automate processes, improve implementations, and create more efficient solutions.

My goal is to continue growing without setting aside the experience I’ve built as a web developer, but rather to use it as a foundation for exploring new technologies and finding new ways to solve problems. In the end, that’s what I’ve enjoyed most about software development ever since that first “Hello World”: the opportunity to constantly learn, turn an idea into something functional, and keep discovering new ways to build.
